title: Steak Sandwiches
shortDescription: Thin-sliced steak, toasted roll, hall classic
subtitle: Thin-sliced steak, toasted roll, hall classic
description: Grill marks, melted cheese, sandwich line

steps.title: Season & rest steak (no heat, 10 min)
steps.instruction: Pat steaks dry; salt and pepper generously. Let sit at room temp while ovens and grill heat.

steps.title: Roast vegetables (425°F, 22 min)
steps.instruction: Toss peppers and zucchini with oil, salt, and garlic. Spread on sheet pans; roast until charred edges and tender.

steps.title: Grill steak (high, 12 min)
steps.instruction: Grill sirloin or flank to medium-rare/medium (130–140°F). Rest 8 minutes, then slice thin against the grain.

steps.title: Garlic fries & onion rings (425°F, 20 min)
steps.instruction: Bake fries until crisp; toss hot fries with butter and minced garlic. Bake onion rings on a second rack if serving.

steps.title: Sauté onions & mushrooms (medium-high, 10 min)
steps.instruction: Cook sliced onions until golden; add mushrooms until browned. Hold warm for the toppings bar.

steps.title: Build Caesar & aioli (no heat, 10 min)
steps.instruction: Toss romaine with dressing, croutons, and parmesan. Mix horseradish into mayo for aioli; keep cold.

steps.title: Toast buns & run sandwich line (serve)
steps.instruction: Split and toast rolls. Layer steak, optional provolone melt, onions, mushrooms, and aioli. Fries, Caesar, and veg on the counter.

proTips: Slice steak thin after the rest — crew eats better and portions stretch.
Toast buns hard enough to hold juice without falling apart.
Keep Caesar and aioli on ice until the line opens.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Steak Sandwiches with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Steak Sandwiches on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thin-sliced steak, toasted roll, hall classic. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
